extra_quotes: Bonded interfaces were made by placing two pieces of clean z-cut LNO single crystal on top of one another, with a relative twist in the orientations of their primary a-b crystallographic axes.

Once bonded, cross-sections were cut and polished to allow focused ion beam milling of thin electron-transparent lamellae, incorporating the interface, with lamellar planar normals at a slight angle to the crystallographic c-axes of the LNO (fig. 1a).
For DPC imaging, a segmented detector (ThermoFisher) was used to measure deflection of the transmitted electron beam.

4DSTEM was acquired on a double-corrected JEOL ARM200F operating at 200 kV, in Nanobeam STEM mode, with a 3 mrad semi-convergence angle and equipped with a Quantum Detectors Merlin pixelated detector.
Multislice ptychographic reconstructions were performed using PtyRAD [42], employing five probe modes, a slice thickness of 0.4 nm, and more than 1,000 iterations.
The transport simulations down twisted multilayers employ the Hairy Probes method for electronic open boundaries [43].

Second-harmonic generation (SHG) experiments are conducted using a mode-locked Ti:sapphire oscillator delivering 100 fs laser pulses at a central wavelength of 800 nm and a repetition rate of 80 MHz in an inverted optical microscope, with detection in a back-reflection geometry as described in Ref. [https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0037286].
